title: Fix bash '[: ==: unary operator expected' in an if-test
summary: Bash prints this error when a variable inside an if [ ... ] test is empty or contains spaces, so the test loses an argument and fails. Putting double quotes around the variable keeps it as one word and fixes the test.

aliases.text: bash too many arguments in if
shell script if test variable error
bash test command breaks with empty variable
ошибка unary operator expected в скрипте
bash too many arguments ошибка в if
баш скрипт ошибка в условии if

prerequisites: A bash script (or a command) with an if [ ... ] test that compares a variable

steps.explain: Find the test line in your script. Look for '[ $' followed by a variable name without quotes. grep prints the line number first.

placeholders.name: SCRIPT
placeholders.description: The script file that shows the error

steps.expect: One or more lines such as 3:if [ $name == "bob" ]; then, with the line number before the colon.

steps.explain: Open the script in a text editor and go to that line. Put double quotes around the variable and use a single = for string comparison, for example if [ "$name" = "bob" ]; then. Save the file.
Check the fixed comparison with an empty variable. The test should print no and no error.
steps.cmd: name=; [ "$name" = bob ] && echo yes || echo no

alternatives.explain: Check the same comparison with a value that contains a space. The quotes keep it as one word, so no 'too many arguments' error appears.
alternatives.cmd: name="Anna Smith"; [ "$name" = bob ] && echo yes || echo no

verify.cmd: name=; [ "$name" = bob ] && echo yes || echo no
verify.expect: Prints no, and no line with 'unary operator expected' appears.

source.title: bash manual; card written and verified in the lnxhelp sandbox
